subject: Urgent: Investigating p99 queueing cascade impacting UpliftCommerce - exec loop
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <ops@upliftcommerce.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: SaaS Support <support@upliftcommerce.com>
Date: 2028-07-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [Uplift] Sudden p99 spikes / request pile-up in checkout pipeline

Connor —

We're seeing repeated p99 spikes and a backlog of pending requests on the Redwood endpoint powering our checkout personalization (route: /v1/generate). The issue started around 08:55 PDT. Customers report slow checkouts and timeouts. Attached are a small sample of traces and request IDs.

Key symptoms:
- p50 stable, p95 mildly elevated, p99 jumping to 4-5s in waves
- backlog count on our side climbs rapidly, then clears intermittently
- errors: ~0.3% 504s and some 429s we think are coming from upstream concurrency caps

Can you confirm whether this is a capacity/backpressure problem or something on our integration? This is impacting conversion — we need a fast path update and ETA.

—Alex
Ops, Uplift Commerce

Attachments:
- sample_traces_0800-0900.json (log snippet)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <ops@upliftcommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-17T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Uplift] Sudden p99 spikes / request pile-up in checkout pipeline

Hi Alex — thanks for the data. I’m opening an internal investigation now and will loop in engineering and account leadership. Initial ask: can you share a few representative request IDs (we'll trace them through logs) and confirm the request QPS and any recent config changes on your side?

Marissa / Kim — I’m putting this on your radar; Uplift is in a high-velocity trial and this is hitting checkout, so we should treat this as an at-risk expansion.

I’ll come back with an initial triage in 30–45m.

—Connor
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-17T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Triage notes — possible queueing + concurrency cap interplay

Team — quick notes from initial check (10:05):

- Telemetry: we see matching symptom windows in our edge logs for Uplift's tenant: spikes in in-flight requests and sudden increases in tokenization latency for some long-context requests.
- Concurrency: their route is pinned to a model variant with a 12-concurrency cap at the Dedicated pool; recent autoscaler activity shows transient node pressure and two short OOM restarts earlier today (02:20 UTC).
- Backpressure behaviour: when capacity hits cap, requests are queued by the fronting router; we see queue length climb then an occasional drain that correlates with a drop in throughput (likely a fallback or limited worker availability).

Immediate asks:
1) Connor — ask Uplift for 3 example request IDs (they provided some; request they send 5) and confirm whether they're sending bursts (batching from their side).
2) David — can infra check if any deployment rollback or kernel change was rolled in the last 6 hours to the pool serving their tenant? Also share p99 traces.
3) Marissa — preparing a concise customer-facing update; flag to execs if this stretches beyond the morning.

Attaching a short snapshot (concurrency_policy_snapshot.txt) and a sample set of traces we pulled (uplift_p99_traces_20280717.zip).

—Kim
Principle SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- uplift_p99_traces_20280717.zip
- concurrency_policy_snapshot.txt
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-17T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Triage notes — possible queueing + concurrency cap interplay

Quick infra readout (11:12):

- No config rollouts in the serving pool for the past 8 hours. Kernel selection unchanged.
- Observed two transient worker restarts in node-group gp-5 (2028-07-17T02:18Z and 2028-07-17T02:24Z). Root cause was a memory pressure spike traced to a long-context request pattern — garbage collection delayed reclaiming KV cache memory; we applied an emergency nudge (rebalanced KV allocations) at 02:30Z.
- Autoscaler response: scaled up 2 nodes at 02:36Z, but warmup lag meant effective capacity increase delayed by ~90s. During that window, router-level queues reached ~420 requests for the tenant and we recorded elevated p99s.

Mitigation steps taken (in-flight):
- Temporarily increased concurrency cap for Uplift's route from 12 -> 18 for the next 2 hours to relieve queued backlog.
- Enabled more aggressive early-KV-eviction for the affected pool to free memory for pending requests.
- Setting up a short-lived canary ramp to validate stability.

Impact note: the temporary cap increase may increase tail latencies on other tenants hosted on the same pool marginally — we need to surface this to PM/exec if customers notice.

Recommendation: prepare executive note and a rollback plan if we see error rates or OOMs increase.

—David
Principal Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <ops@upliftcommerce.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-18T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Uplift] Sudden p99 spikes / request pile-up in checkout pipeline — status update

Alex —

Thanks for your patience. Quick summary and next steps:

What happened: transient memory pressure on the Dedicated pool serving your tenant led to worker restarts and a short window where router queues accumulated. That produced the p99 spikes and some 504/429 symptoms while capacity caught up.

What we did:
- Increased concurrency cap temporarily to 18 to drain the backlog and reduced KV cache residency to prioritize active requests.
- Autoscaler brought nodes up; we observed queue clear after the warmup delay.
- We also captured traces and a sample set of impacted request IDs and attached them to this thread for your ops team.

Where we're going next:
1) Engineering (David & Kim) are implementing a safer early-eviction heuristic and a smoother node warmup policy; ETA for deploy: 2028-07-21.
2) We will monitor your route closely for 24h and will revert the temporary cap if we see elevated error rates.
3) Connor and I will sync with your procurement lead about options for Dedicated capacity isolation if you expect sustained bursty patterns — this reduces noisy-neighbor effects.

We appreciate the signal — apologies for the impact. Please send any additional request IDs (or a short list of problematic timestamps) and we'll prioritize those traces.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
